statusText: Calm, pre-event positioning roughly 55-60 minutes ahead of today's 12:30 UTC Retail Sales / 14:00 UTC preliminary UMich cluster. The S&P 500 closed at a fresh record above 7,800 on Thursday (+0.65%) and Asia-Pacific markets extended gains Friday on continued AI/chip-sector strength. Heading into the U.S. cash open, premarket Nasdaq-100 futures reads conflict across sources -- one read shows futures modestly higher while another shows them slipping just below flat -- rather than showing persistent one-way structure, so Tail stays anchored low. VIX holds flat-to-firm near 14.6-14.7 and the 10-year Treasury yield is little changed near 4.65%. Oil continues to firm on the unresolved Strait of Hormuz standoff (WTI ~$81.3, Brent ~$89.5) with no confirmed new kinetic escalation identified today -- Iran's self-declared 'Persian Gulf Strait Authority' passage-permit regime and intermittent vessel harassment remain the same brinkmanship backdrop as prior runs. Alpha Vantage was rate-limited on both the initial call and an immediate retry, so this assessment again relies entirely on WebSearch; the cross-source disagreement on the exact premarket futures print (an early sign of thin, still-forming pre-open liquidity) keeps Confidence in the low band.
recommendation: Current action remains EA_ON. Tail stays in the low band because no persistent one-way price-path structure has been observed in the Nasdaq-100 complex itself -- the mixed/conflicting premarket futures reads are not evidence of directional efficiency. Stress is building modestly into the 12:30 UTC Retail Sales and 14:00 UTC UMich sentiment cluster and the U.S. cash open shortly after; existing-position management and emergency protection remain active through that window regardless of the current EA_ON state. An upgrade to a higher Tail state would require an observed failed-pullback/repeated-extension reaction in NQ itself after the data prints, not the pending releases, the unresolved Hormuz backdrop, or this run's Alpha Vantage outage on their own.

body: At 11:33 UTC, roughly 55-60 minutes ahead of the 12:30 UTC Retail Sales print, conditions remain calm and largely two-sided heading into the U.S. cash open. The S&P 500 closed Thursday at a fresh record above 7,800 (+0.65% to 7,798.99) on cooler-than-expected inflation data, and Asia-Pacific markets extended those gains into Friday's session on continued AI/chip-sector strength, with South Korea's Kospi up over 1.4% and Japan's Nikkei adding roughly 0.8%. Heading into the cash open, premarket Nasdaq-100 futures reads conflict across sources: one read shows S&P 500 futures little changed with Nasdaq-100 futures slipping just below the flat line and Dow futures up about 0.1%, while a separate prediction-market read puts the odds of a higher S&P 500 open at roughly 57%. This is a single-hour continuation of the mixed/roughly-flat premarket tone already present in the prior run, not a new directional signal, and the cross-source disagreement itself is treated as evidence of thin, still-forming pre-open liquidity rather than as a Tail input. VIX holds flat-to-firm near 14.6-14.7, essentially unchanged from the prior run's 14.5-14.75 range, and the 10-year Treasury yield remains anchored near 4.65% with no material move since Thursday's close. Oil continues to firm on the unresolved Strait of Hormuz standoff: WTI trades near $81.3 and Brent near $89.5 (up from the prior run's $87.9-88.0 read), as diplomatic efforts to fully reopen the strait remain stalled, Iran's self-declared 'Persian Gulf Strait Authority' continues to assert a passage-permit regime, and Saudi Arabia/UAE reportedly explore alternative export routes with some vessels switching off transponders while transiting. No confirmed new kinetic escalation (fresh strike, vessel seizure, or full closure) was identified for today specifically -- this is the same protracted brinkmanship backdrop noted in prior runs, now showing through in a firmer oil print rather than a fresh discontinuity. Retail Sales (July, 8:30am ET / 12:30 UTC) is the session's first checkpoint, with consensus estimates clustered around +0.1% to +0.3% MoM headline and +0.2% ex-auto, followed by preliminary University of Michigan consumer sentiment at 10am ET / 14:00 UTC and the U.S. cash open at 9:30am ET / 13:30 UTC sitting between the two prints. Alpha Vantage's TREASURY_YIELD call was rate-limited on both the initial attempt and an immediate retry, continuing the outage seen across recent runs, so per the fallback protocol this assessment again relies entirely on WebSearch for yields, oil, VIX, equities, and price-path context; the conflicting premarket futures reads across sources this run keep Confidence in the low band, roughly flat versus the prior run. Tail holds at 9% (low) because no persistent one-way price-path structure -- shallow/no pullbacks, repeated extension after failed retracements, or NQ holding near session extremes -- has been observed in the Nasdaq-100 complex itself; the mixed premarket reads are evidence of two-sided positioning, not pathological directional efficiency. Stress firms to 33% (moderate, up from 28% in the prior run) reflecting the closer proximity to the Retail Sales/UMich data cluster and the cash open, plus the continued cross-asset tension from firmer oil against flat VIX/yields, with Stress projected to build further into the mid-40s through the print and cash-open window before easing back through the afternoon and into the quiet weekend handover.

lookbackSummary: Tail held in the low band (9-18%) through the full prior 24 hours as the index ground to a fresh S&P 500 record above 7,800 on soft CPI/PPI prints; Stress ran elevated to high (up to 58%) around the Wednesday/Thursday CPI-PPI and earnings window before easing back into the moderate band (25-33%) through Friday's European morning as the after-hours reaction stayed contained to single names and no broader transmission was confirmed.
outlookSummary: Tail is projected to stay low (4-11%) through the next 24 hours; Stress is projected to build from the low-30s toward the mid-40s across the 12:30-14:00 UTC Retail Sales/UMich cluster and the U.S. cash-open/power-hour window before easing back through the evening and into the quiet Saturday handover, with no forecast slot currently implying an action change from EA_ON. Confidence is projected to stay in the low band throughout, reflecting the continued Alpha Vantage outage and this run's cross-source premarket disagreement.
